demand_source.title: Memory overview (OpenClaw docs)
demand_source.supports: OpenClaw's memory guide presents asking the agent to remember a fact, which it then writes to its memory files, as the normal way to use memory.

edits.description: A parent texts 'remember that...' and their own agent writes the fact to its notes and finds it again in later chats. Where those notes live is an open decision that settles two things: whether a saved note survives the next deploy, and whether it is in view at the start of a chat or found only when Happy searches.
edits.how:
Allow write/edit (deny apply_patch) on

-main with rw workspace; an in-house before_tool_call hook limits write paths, by default to memory/*.md only (MEMORY.md and USER.md stay with the F042 generator unless a live test shows that a chat write does not stop them loading); memory_search FTS-only; session-memory hook.
caveats: Where chat-saved notes live is undecided, and the installed version gives a reason to keep them out of MEMORY.md and USER.md. OpenClaw records, file by file, where a memory file's last write came from. A write made in a turn from a sender who is not the command owner (the roadmap makes Tony the only one, so every turn of Jordan's counts), or after web content in the same turn, marks the whole file untrusted; so does a second chat write to a file that the family-facts generator (F042) has re-rendered since the first. An untrusted MEMORY.md or USER.md is no longer loaded at the start of a chat, the generated family facts in it included, although search still finds it (memory-architecture.md:112 and :217; dist/agent-tools-D5UK6LHM.mjs:496; dist/memory-artifact-provenance-D8JQrziA.mjs:76). This was read in the installed docs and code and not tried on a live turn.

Keeping saved notes in memory/*.md only avoids that but has its own cost: of the dated notes only today's and yesterday's load at a fresh start, and older ones are found only when the agent searches (memory.md:22, memory-architecture.md:54). Until the choice is made and tested for both parents, a saved note is not guaranteed to come back, and F042 expects a chat edit to a generated file to be lost at the next deploy.
Search is by keyword only until local embeddings are added (F046), so a saved note is found by its words, not by its meaning.

MEMORY.md is loaded at the start of a parent's one-to-one chat but not in scheduled jobs, group chats or hand-offs to a helper (user-model.md:376), so a brief or a reminder does not know a saved note unless its job is given memory search.

The planned refusal of memory writes in a turn that carried web or research results is not something the platform does for a file write. OpenClaw does mark the rest of a turn as tainted once a tool result declares web content, and classifies memory from that turn as untrusted (memory-architecture.md:117), but the docs opened describe this as a label used for promotion and for loading, and their advice for preventing a write is to restrict the file tools (memory-provenance.md:182). No taint flag that a hook can read was found, so the hook would have to track web tool calls itself. Untested.
Notes belong to one parent. Something both parents should get the same answer to belongs in the household store (F031) or the family handbook (F043).
Later option if saved notes and search prove too weak: Active Memory's recall across conversations, which adds a blocking model call to each reply it runs on.
depends_on: Decision: where chat-saved notes live. Working default: memory/*.md only, because a chat write to MEMORY.md or USER.md can stop that file, and the family facts F042 renders into it, from loading at the start of a chat (see caveats)
An in-house before_tool_call hook that limits write and edit to the chosen memory files, proven with a test write outside them; apply_patch denied by name
memory_search and memory_get allowed on each parent's agent, with keyword-only search

A live test for each parent before go-live: save a note, start a new chat, and check that the note is found and that the family facts still load; include one note saved in Chinese. For Jordan the result may turn on whether she is made a command owner, the decision listed under timed reminders (F007)
unverified: Whether visibility 'self' already reaches the same chat's pre-reset history (the docs define self as the current session key) was not tested.

No taint flag that a plugin hook can read was found in the hook docs opened, although OpenClaw's memory design does mark a turn as tainted after web content (memory-architecture.md:117); so 'refuse writes after web results' means the hook tracking web tool calls itself. Untested.

How a direct agent write to a memory file is classified was read in the installed code, not seen on a live turn: the write is recorded as agent-written only in a command owner's turn with no web content, and only if the file has not changed since its last recorded write; otherwise the whole file is recorded as untrusted (dist/agent-tools-D5UK6LHM.mjs:496, dist/memory-artifact-provenance-D8JQrziA.mjs:76). MEMORY.md and USER.md load at the start of a chat only while their record counts as eligible (memory-architecture.md:215). Check on a live turn for each parent.
Whether a note saved in one of Jordan's turns (she is not the command owner) comes back from memory_search like any other note, or is shown to the model with an untrusted label, was not tested.
Whether the F042 generator keeps lines Happy saved by chat was not checked; the generator was not opened.

Whether keyword search finds a note saved in Chinese on the default index setting was not tested: the engine page lists Chinese support through trigram tokenization (memory-builtin.md:23), the config reference gives `unicode61` as the default tokenizer with `trigram` as the alternative (reference/memory-config.md:625), and the search guide's fix for Chinese text that is not found is a forced re-index (memory-search.md:226). F042's own example has Jordan writing to Happy in Chinese, so the live test should include one such note.

How an untrusted label is cleared once it is set was not found: in the code read, the label recorded for a file is returned without comparing it with the file's current contents (dist/memory-path-provenance-BiFQlpIk.mjs:49), so a re-render by the generator may not bring a file back into the start of a chat.

From family.json5 the generator renders each adult's directives into USER.md (4,000-character cap), the per-person reply-language line among them (G011), and the kid and routine facts into MEMORY.md with trigger comments (F042); nothing is rendered into shared agents. caveats: Asking Happy to save a skill from iMessage does not work on this stack: sandboxed runs do not construct the `skill_workshop` tool, and the documented exception would publish with no pending draft and so skip Tony's review, which is one more reason to keep that tool off every family agent.
A skill is know-how: it cannot add tools or accounts, so 'learn to order the groceries' still ends at a list.

A skill is instruction text loaded into future sessions, so one written from a pasted web page or an email is a stored injection: author only from the parent's own words, and install no marketplace skills (an audit reported by The Hacker News found 341 malicious entries among 2,857 ClawHub skills in early 2026).

Turnaround is 'when Tony next deploys', and Happy does not run a skill every time: the prompt lists only each skill's name and one-line description, so that line has to be precise, and calling the skill by name (`/skill <name>`) is the sure route where that command is accepted from the sender.

The quiz is parent-run only: the kids are not users, the parent holds the phone and sends the answers, and a version a child uses alone waits for the kids agent (F072) and never uses a cloud model or cloud speech.

The ChatGPT or Gemini app on a parent's phone already makes a quiz from uploaded material, with hints and an end summary; Happy's only edge is that it lives in the same thread and can schedule the re-quiz.
Models write wrong answer keys, especially for arithmetic and for facts the sheet does not state, so tell it to quiz only from what is on the page and spot-check.

A text quiz shows spelling words on screen, so spelling practice needs the words read aloud with the local voice (F003), whose quality for spelling words is untried, and the running score lives in the conversation and is gone after the daily session reset.

Once per-person memory (F041) gives a parent's agent `write` and `edit` on a read-write workspace, the workspace skills folder sits inside what the agent can write: for that mode the docs describe a read-only copy only for bundled, managed and plugin skills (workspace-access.md:91) and do not say the workspace skills folder is protected. 'No model-written file reaches a skills folder' then rests on F041's in-house path hook, so that hook's proof must include a refused write to skills/.
edits.safety: Operator review is the gate: `skill_workshop` stays denied on every family agent, a skill cannot widen tool policy, and no model-written file is meant to reach a skills folder. Once per-person memory (F041) lets the same agent write files in its workspace, that last point rests on F041's write-path hook and has to be proven with a refused write to skills/. The quiz is the riskier part: a photographed school worksheet is untrusted content, is not screened by the PDF privacy gate in F002, and goes to the cloud vision model under store:false. No child's account talks to a cloud model.

edits.safety: The mail agent holds private mail and reads untrusted mail text, so it gets no way out of its own: no web, file, code or browser tools, no draft or send tool, and texts only to the mailbox's owner. The digest runs unattended on that same agent. The lookup is the weaker half: its answer returns into the parent's own agent, which holds that parent's memory and can hand a task to the research helper, so a mail written to mislead could reach the hand-off that the roadmap names as its one remaining leak path. The relayed answer has to be treated as untrusted (a prompt rule, not an enforced limit), and a seeded-mail test has to show that it cannot make the parent's agent pass anything to research. The other open question is the model: personal mail would go to the cloud model.
caveats: The roadmap's M4 keeps each inbox on a local model and none is installed, so the lookup and the digest both send personal mail to the cloud model, and without Zero Data Retention the 30-day abuse-monitoring log applies to that text; this is Tony's open decision and the whole card waits on it.

Google already does much of this where the mail lives: the Gemini app answers questions from a person's own Gmail and lists a daily digest of calendar, to-dos and emails among its scheduled actions, and Gmail's 'AI Inbox' was announced in January 2026, so try those on one parent's account before building; Happy adds only asking, and being told, in the iMessage thread.
gog is not installed on this Mac, so its flags come from upstream docs and must be confirmed with `gog mcp --list-tools` and `gog auth add --help` on the installed version.
With sandbox mode all, MCP tools stay hidden unless `tools.sandbox.tools` names `bundle-mcp` or the server glob, and the minimal profile does not allow MCP tools implicitly.

A Google sign-in app left in Testing issues tokens that expire after seven days, so the app is published to In production (the consent screen then shows a warning) or each adult signs in again every week; whether both adults' tokens can share one keyring under the happy user is still open.

'Send pinned to owner' applies only when the mail agent runs its own scheduled turn, because a mail agent spawned from `

-main` always loses `message` and `session_status`; that a before_tool_call hook reaches MCP tool calls is implied by the docs but not stated.
'Memory off' is not one switch: memory search has a per-agent override, dreaming is plugin-wide, and the session-exclusion setting only matches hook sessions.

Reply drafts are left out, 'subject line only for health senders' and 'do not open the form' are instructions to the agent and not enforced limits, and the tax-form check only knows that a notice email arrived, so a form that came by post or sits in a portal shows as missing.

The lookup goes one step beyond the roadmap's design, where a mail agent's only output is its scheduled text to the owner: here the answer comes back into the parent's own agent, which holds that parent's notes and may hand a task to the research helper (F019). OpenClaw's guidance is to deny `sessions_spawn` to an agent that handles untrusted content (tool-permissions.md:21), and the roadmap already names that hand-off as its one remaining leak path, so the lookup needs its own test with a seeded misleading mail, or the card can start with the digest alone.

edits.safety: The design keeps the children's content off the cloud: the agent, its classifiers and the digest summariser are local, and with the classifier down the agent answers 'ask a grown-up'. Alerts carry a category, not the child's words. Two points are open. The nightly digest tells the parents what a child asked and is delivered into a parent's chat with Happy; OpenClaw copies a scheduled delivery into a session transcript, and if that session belongs to a parent's cloud-backed agent the child's words would reach the cloud model, so the delivery route has to be checked before the digest quotes anything. And the speaker's bridge: the chat endpoint is equivalent to an operator secret, so the speaker must reach only the tool-less kids agent.
caveats: Blocked until a local model and local classifiers exist and the kid-safety evals pass, because kids' content never goes to a cloud model or cloud speech.

A local classifier's accuracy on how 8 and 10-year-olds actually write is unproven: false alarms will annoy, misses matter more, and a home system has no human reviewer between the flag and the parent notice.

Common Sense Media rated Google's supervised assistant for under-13s high risk and recommends that children aged 6 to 12 use chatbots only under adult supervision; an alert and an evening digest are a look afterwards, not supervision, so whether a child may chat alone is a decision to take before building.
'Refuse whole-worksheet answers' is a prompt rule, and no source shows a model holds to it when a child pushes.
The alert is a heads-up to parents and not a crisis service, and the parents should be told so.

The speaker has no interim adult version: nothing identifies who is speaking, so without a local model a child's question would reach OpenAI as text, and speech stays in the house only while Home Assistant's own cloud speech option is left off.

The hop from Home Assistant to Happy is unsolved: Home Assistant's official OpenAI integration only talks to OpenAI's own endpoint, and with token auth OpenClaw's chat endpoint gives the caller the full operator scope set and lets the request choose the agent, so the bridge would be a community integration or a self-written kids-only shim.

The speaker adds an always-on VM to patch and back up, Home Assistant itself calls the device a preview, and open-ended questions need Whisper, which Home Assistant recommends only on powerful hardware.
How the safety plugin texts the parents from inside a hook is not settled: no plugin-side send path was found in the hook docs read, so an 'immediate' alert is the aim, not a tested behaviour.
depends_on: a local model and local safety classifiers (the roadmap's M2, currently skipped)
the kid-safety evals passing
each kid having an own Apple child account and handle (text route)
G009 family delivery primitive
decision: whether a child may chat with Happy alone or only with a parent alongside (Common Sense Media recommends adult supervision for ages 6 to 12)
for the speaker: the device ($69 on Home Assistant's page; the roadmap says $59) and a Home Assistant OS VM on the Mac (the same VM the later Home Assistant option for house devices, F076, would use)
for the speaker: a scoped endpoint or kids-only shim between Home Assistant and the gateway
